title: Reduced-Word-Size Integral Characteristic Bounds
summary: Longer integral characteristics have been observed only at 4- or 5-bit word sizes; whether reduced-size maxima upper-bound and closely approximate unreduced maxima remains conjectural.

formal_statement.body: When division-property-based integral characteristics are computed using reduced word sizes, the optimization can yield longer characteristics, but this side effect has been observed only for very small word sizes of $4$ or $5$ bits. Determine whether, in these cases, the resulting maximum characteristic lengths are upper bounds on the corresponding maximum lengths obtainable without reducing the word size and whether the reduced-word-size values are close to the unreduced values.

scope.domain: Division-property-based integral cryptanalysis using reduced-word-size computation.
parameters: Word size: distinguishes the reduced computation, including the observed 4- and 5-bit cases, from the unreduced computation
Maximum integral-characteristic length: the quantity compared between reduced and unreduced word sizes
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether reduced-word-size maximum lengths upper-bound, and are close to, the corresponding unreduced-word-size maxima.

citations.label: Design Strategies for ARX with Provable Bounds: Sparx and LAX

progress.summary: The source reports the longer-characteristic side effect only for 4- and 5-bit word sizes and explicitly conjectures that the resulting values are upper bounds and very close to unreduced-word-size values.
citation_labels: Daniel Dinu et al., Design Strategies for ARX with Provable Bounds: Sparx and LAX
